routes.name: Mount Rainier Mountaineers Route (winter variant)
routes.seasonal_profile: Jan-Mar optimal window (stable snowpack, thicker snow bridges). Nov/Apr transition zones extremely hazardous (crevasse opening, warming effects). Not recommended Jun+.
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Whiteout conditions common; avalanche path crossing critical; Camp Muir weather exposure severe. Wind chill -20°F to -30°F possible at 13,000+ ft.
routes.key_facts: Route changes annually; high-density crevasse fields above 10,000 ft on Ingraham Glacier. Afternoon whiteouts cause orientation errors leading to unroped cliff descents or hidden crevasses. Requires bearing navigation in zero visibility.
sources: RMI Guides - Mount Rainier Climbing Safely
AAC Publications - Danger Zones Mt. Rainier

routes.name: Mount Rainier Camp Muir approach (winter)
routes.seasonal_profile: Dec-Feb optimal (stable snow, good bridge thickness). Mar-Apr transition (warming, bridge deterioration, crevasse opening acceleration). Not recommended May+.
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Microspikes minimum; ice axe essential for self-arrest. Early morning: hard ice; afternoon: slushy/unstable. Wind chill -20°F at 10,188 ft elevation.
routes.key_facts: Crevasses open adjacent to main route, hidden by thin seasonal snow. Particularly dangerous near Anvil Rock (11,200 ft) and McClure Rock zones. Previous bootpacks unreliable. Deaths documented from navigation failures on Muir Snowfield.
sources: Sand and Elevation - Camp Muir Guide

routes.name: Mount Baker Coleman Glacier (winter variant)
routes.seasonal_profile: Mar-Apr optimal (late season, better stability, melt reduces avalanche slab formation). Avoid Nov-Feb (deepest winter instability, highest avalanche probability). Not recommended May+ (thermal activity increases, melt accelerates).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Record snowfall area (28.9 m in 1998-99 winter); seasonal snow depth unpredictable. Maritime influence: temperature fluctuations, rain-on-snow events Dec-Mar. Wind speeds 20+ mph common; slab formation on lee aspects frequent.
routes.key_facts: Notoriously high avalanche danger Dec-Apr; rare safe windows. Coleman Glacier severely crevassed; 100+ square km of glaciers. Thermal venting can trigger sudden avalanches. Lahars documented hazard.
sources: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest - Climbing Safety

routes.name: Mount Baker North Ridge (winter variant)
routes.seasonal_profile: Late Mar-Apr optimal (more stable, earlier season instability passes). Avoid Nov-Feb (highest avalanche/weather instability). Not recommended May+ (melt, thermal activity, hazard multiplication).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Longer, exposed high-altitude passage increases cold exposure (wind chill -20° to -30°F). Shorter day length reduces margin for error; headlamp required for pre-dawn start.
routes.key_facts: Multiple crevasse crossings near summit plateau; large west-face exposure hazard. Snow slopes left of ridge accumulate wind-loaded slabs. Serac activity from Coleman/Deming zone threatens approach.
sources: Mountain Project - Mt. Baker North Ridge

routes.name: North Cascades Cascade Pass (winter approach)
routes.seasonal_profile: Jan-Feb optimal (stable snowpack, road closure containment). Mar-Apr transition (slab danger peaks, melt increases water hazards). Not recommended Apr-Jun (road still closed, melt accelerating, avalanche danger peaks).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Maritime climate: heavy precipitation (rain at mid-elevations, snow above); freezing levels variable. Wind exposure creates wind slab hazard; northeast winds most problematic. Visibility: frequent low clouds, fog; average visibility <100m typical.
routes.key_facts: Cascade River Road closed Nov-Jun typically; closure adds approach miles/hours in deep snow. Slope angles 25-35° within slab-avalanche range. Approach crosses marginal glacier zones; snow bridges over creeks/melt channels.

routes.name: North Cascades Ptarmigan Traverse (winter variant)
routes.seasonal_profile: Winter avoid Dec-Mar (avalanche danger peak, rare safe windows). Transition (ski season) Apr-May optimal (avalanche hazard decreases, snow bridges stabilizing). Early summer Jun (lower avalanche probability; melt hazards increase).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: High-altitude traverse: wind chill -15° to -25°F typical. Visibility: frequent cloud cover; visibility <200m on forecast days. Route-finding: deep snow obliterates markers; compass navigation essential.
routes.key_facts: 'Avalanche conditions unlikely to be favorable for more than a few rare days at a time' in winter. Steep terrain adds traverse miles in deep winter; avalanche risk multiplied by days in exposure. South Cascade Glacier option crosses complex glaciated terrain.

routes.name: Snoqualmie Pass Chair Peak (winter route)
routes.seasonal_profile: Feb-Mar optimal (stable snowpack, avalanche danger lower than early winter). High risk Nov-Jan (deep winter instability, wind loading, slab development). Avoid Apr+ (warming, melt hazard, wet slabs).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Maritime climate instability: rapid weather changes, high precipitation. Wind chill -15° to -20°F at 6,000+ ft elevations. Visibility poor; frequent cloud cover, whiteout risk.
routes.key_facts: 'Entire basin between Alpental Ski Resort and Chair Peak extremely avalanche prone'. Fatal slides documented historically. Steep open chutes (Chair, Kaleetan, Bryant peaks) funnel avalanche debris. 'Some of the best moderate alpine ice climbs in region' in winter conditions.
sources: Climber Kyle - Snoqualmie Pass Ice Climbs

routes.name: Snoqualmie Pass Kaleetan Peak (winter access)
routes.seasonal_profile: Feb-Mar optimal (lower avalanche probability than early winter). High risk transitions Nov-Jan and Apr-May (instability peaks and warming effects).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Maritime instability creates varied conditions; equipment (ice axe, crampons) mandatory. Wind chill severe; exposed ridge traverse at 6,000+ ft. Visibility: frequent clouds, whiteout risk in basin.
routes.key_facts: 'Kaleetan classified part of avalanche-prone basin terrain (with Chair Peak, Bryant)'. Steep chutes funnel avalanche hazard; slope angles exceed 30° in main approach. 'Ice axe, crampons and a rope recommended when going to summit'.
sources: Hike Seeker - Ultimate Guide to Snoqualmie Pass Hikes

routes.name: Stevens Pass winter ski/snowshoe access (Tye Creek area)
routes.seasonal_profile: Feb-Mar optimal (relatively stable avalanche conditions). High risk Nov-Jan and Apr-May (transitions, instability peaks).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Maritime Pacific influence: variable temps, high precipitation, rain-on-snow events. Tye Mill area wind measurement shows typical 15-25 mph gusts. Visibility: frequent cloud cover; whiteout common above 5,000 ft.
routes.key_facts: '230+ named avalanche paths' on peak. Beyond ski area boundary: no avalanche control or patrol; rescue not guaranteed. 'Rescue from these areas not guaranteed and if available, may be slow and costly'.
sources: Stevens Pass Ski Resort - Mountain Safety

routes.name: Enchantments Cashmere/Aasgard Pass (winter approach)
routes.seasonal_profile: Feb-Mar optimal (stable snow, thicker bridges, lower melt hazard). Apr-May high risk (warming, bridge deterioration accelerates, wet slabs form). Not recommended Jun+ (melt hazards dominate; blue ice melts; crevasse exposure increases).
routes.winter_specific_conditions: High alpine exposure: wind chill -15° to -20°F typical. Frequent cloud cover; visibility <200m on forecast days common. Snow depth variable; standard route becomes bushwhacking in low-snow years.
routes.key_facts: 'Route climbs through avalanche-prone slopes particularly on climb up Lake Vivian and down Aasgard Pass'. Blue ice waterfall forms in center of slope (hazard marker). Historical incident (1998): 30-foot fall through bridge on Aasgard Pass glissade.
sources: The Mountaineers - Unseen Danger: Snow Bridge Hazards
WTA - Snow Lakes, Colchuck Lake, Enchantments Trip Report

routes.name: Spring Transition Routes (All WA alpine; Mar-May hazards)
routes.db_search_pattern: All WA alpine routes with spring climbing activity
routes.seasonal_profile: Mar (early spring): Stable snowpack, good bridge thickness, persistent slabs still present (hazard moderate). Apr (mid-spring): Warming accelerates; wet loose/slab probability rises; bridges weaken daily. May (late spring): Peak melt hazard; bridges fail; objective hazards (rockfall) multiply.
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Aspect-dependent hazard: south-facing slopes hazardous midday; north aspects safer early morning. Visibility: afternoon clouds form; route-finding becomes secondary safety concern. Wind chill still severe at high elevation despite warming trend at mid-elevations.
routes.key_facts: 'Winterlike conditions can extend well into March and April'. Multiple buried weak layers persist into March; slab propagation documented across large distances. Bridges thicken through mid-winter, peak thickness late Feb-early Mar. Warming trends Apr-May accelerate deterioration.
sources: Mountaineers - Spring Hazards to Plan Around
Mount Washington Avalanche Center - Springtime Hazards

routes.name: Fall Transition Routes (All WA alpine; Sept-Oct hazards)
routes.db_search_pattern: All WA alpine routes with fall climbing activity
routes.seasonal_profile: Sept (early fall): Generally safe; occasional early storms; new snow avalanche hazard emerging. Oct (mid-fall): High-risk window; early snow probable; access closures frequent; conditions volatile. Late Oct+: Alpine access limited; early winter conditions; snow consolidation begins.
routes.winter_specific_conditions: Temperature swings: 40°F to freezing common same-day swings. Precipitation transition: rain → snow line variable; often strands climbers in wet conditions transitioning to snow. Wind chill: accelerates rapidly with elevation gain; exposed terrain hazardous.
routes.key_facts: Shorter days, colder nights drive quick weather pattern changes; early storms possible. Snoqualmie Pass documented early-season snowfall records; highway closures typical Sept-Oct. New snow on warm ground creates weak layer instability.
sources: Snoqualmie Pass Early Season Snowfall Records
Pacific Northwest National Scenic Trail - Snow Information
